intended_object: The circulant matrix generated by a vector v: the matrix whose (i, j) entry is v_{(i−j) mod n} (from the docstring and the name).
explanation: The body `of fun i j => v (i - j)` matches the standard convention C_{jk} = c_{(j−k) mod n} (as on Wikipedia), in which v is the first column of the matrix. Some books, such as Davis's, put v in the first row instead (v (j - i)). That matrix is the transpose of this one and is also circulant, so the two conventions describe the same class of matrices. The definition only needs subtraction on the index type (`[Sub n]`) and works for any entry type α. For `Fin n` it gives the classical circulant matrix, and for an additive group it gives the usual G-circulant generalisation. This is at least as general as the notion in the literature, so it is not too narrow.
